## Zenodo API

```{r}
# test example
  zenodo_request <- request("https://zenodo.org/api") %>%
    req_url_path_append("records") %>%
    req_url_query(q = "null result penalty")%>%
    req_url_query(sort = "bestmatch", size = 1, type = "dataset")
  
  # Pull Data
  zenodo <- req_perform(zenodo_request)
  
  # Flatten and extract resulting datasets
  zenodo_tbl <- zenodo %>%
    resp_body_json(simplifyVector = TRUE, flatten = TRUE)

  results <- zenodo_tbl$hits$hits #$title, $doi_url, etc. just pull first one? was there a query to just pull first hit i feel like there was?
  glimpse(results)
```

```{r}
#my_key <- readLines("zenodo_api_key.txt") # don't think i even need
# Loop over all articles
for(i in 1:length(papers)) {
  print(i)
  # Respect zenodo rate limit of 60/minute
  if(i%%30 == 0) Sys.sleep(60)
  # 314, 490, 540, 624 seemed to have a bug = 500 internal server error
  
  # Generate request URL
  zenodo_request <- request("https://zenodo.org/api") %>%
    req_url_path_append("records") %>%
    req_url_query(q = papers[i])%>%
    req_url_query(sort = "bestmatch", type = "dataset", size = 1)
  
  # Flatten and extract resulting datasets
  zenodo_tbl <- req_perform(zenodo_request) %>%
    resp_body_json(simplifyVector = TRUE, flatten = TRUE)

  dataset <- zenodo_tbl$hits$hits #$title, $doi_url, etc. just pull first one? was there a query to just pull first hit i feel like there was?
  if(length(dataset)==0) {
    next
  }
  
  # Store findings
  brodeur_articles[i, 'zenURL'] <- dataset$doi_url
  brodeur_articles[i, 'zenName'] <- dataset$title
}
```

## Dataverse API

```{r}
for(i in 1:length(papers)){
  #482, 483
print(i)
# Format request
  dataverse_request <- request("https://dataverse.harvard.edu/api") %>%
  req_url_path_append("search") %>%
  req_url_query(q = papers[i]) %>%
  req_url_query(sort = "score", type = "dataset", per_page = 1)
  
# Perform request, flatten
  dataverse_tbl <- req_perform(dataverse_request) %>%
    resp_body_json(simplifyVector = TRUE, flatten = TRUE)
  
# Skip if no results
  if(length(dataverse_tbl$data$items) == 0){
    next
  }
  
# Extract results of interest
  dataset <- dataverse_tbl$data$items %>%
    select(c(name, url))

# Store findings
  brodeur_articles[i, 'dvURL'] <- dataset$url
  brodeur_articles[i, 'dvName'] <- dataset$name
}

#write.csv(brodeur_articles, "articlesWithMatchesTemp.csv")
```

## ICPSR Collection

I tried to use the `icpsrdata` R package, but it seems to require a file_id. So we will scrape the old fashioned way.

```{r}
get_icpsr_scrape <- function(search_term) {
  
  encoded_term <- utils::URLencode(search_term)
  
  target_url <- paste0(
    "https://www.icpsr.umich.edu/sites/icpsr/search/studies?fq=ARCHIVE%3Aopenicpsr&q=", 
    encoded_term
  )
  
  tryCatch({
    # Build request using httr2 with realistic browser signatures
    req <- httr2::request(target_url) %>% 
      httr2::req_timeout(15) %>% 
      httr2::req_headers(
        `User-Agent` = "Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36",
        `Accept` = "text/html,application/xhtml+xml,application/xml;q=0.9,image/webp,*/*;q=0.8",
        `Accept-Language` = "en-US,en;q=0.5"
      )
    
    # Perform the request
    resp <- httr2::req_perform(req)
    
    # Read the HTML body directly from the response object
    page <- httr2::resp_body_html(resp)
    
    # Look for the links that contain study identifiers
    top_hit_link <- page %>% 
      rvest::html_element("a[href*='/icpsrweb/ICPSR/studies/'], a[href*='/openicpsr/project/']")
    
    # If no matching elements are found, return empty strings
    if (length(top_hit_link) == 0 || is.na(top_hit_link)) {
      return(data.frame(icpsrTitle = NA_character_, icpsrURL = NA_character_))
    }
    
    # Extract text and relative URL
    title <- top_hit_link %>% rvest::html_text(trim = TRUE)
    relative_url <- top_hit_link %>% rvest::html_attr("href")
    
    # Standardize the absolute path
    full_url <- if (stringr::str_starts(relative_url, "http")) {
      relative_url
    } else {
      paste0("https://www.icpsr.umich.edu", relative_url)
    }
    
    return(data.frame(icpsrTitle = title, icpsrURL = full_url, stringsAsFactors = FALSE))
    
  }, error = function(e) {
    warning(paste("Error scraping for:", search_term, "-", e$message))
    return(data.frame(icpsrTitle = NA_character_, icpsrURL = NA_character_))
  })
}



icpsr_results <- papers %>% 
  map_dfr(~ {
    Sys.sleep(1.5) 
    get_icpsr_scrape(.x)
  })



# Store findings
  brodeur_articles['icpsrURL'] <- icpsr_results$icpsrURL
  brodeur_articles['icpsrName'] <- icpsr_results$icpsrTitle
#write.csv(brodeur_articles, "articlesWithICPSR.csv")
```

## Fuzzy Text Matching to See if Hits are Actually Relevant

Matching zenName and dvName to title in brodeur_articles

```{r}
brodeur_articles <- read.csv("articlesWithICPSR.csv")
my_custom_words <- c("replication", "data") 

# 3. Create a robust text-cleaning function
clean_text <- function(text, custom_stopwords = c()) {
  if (is.null(text)) return(NA)
  
  text %>%
    # Convert to lowercase
    str_to_lower() %>%
    # Remove quotation marks (both straight and curly)
    str_replace_all('[\'""`‘’“”]', "") %>%
    # Remove other "weird" symbols and punctuation (keep alphanumeric and spaces)
    str_replace_all("[^[:alnum:][:space:]]", " ") %>%
    # Replace multiple spaces/newlines with a single space
    str_replace_all("\\s+", " ") %>%
    # Trim leading and trailing spaces
    str_trim() %>%
    # Remove standard English stop words and custom words
    # (Using regex boundaries \\b to ensure we only match whole words)
    str_remove_all(paste0("\\b(", paste(c(tidytext::stop_words$word, custom_stopwords), collapse = "|"), ")\\b")) %>%
    # Clean up any extra spaces left over after removing words
    str_replace_all("\\s+", " ") %>%
    str_trim()
}

# 5. Clean strings and calculate fuzzy match percentage
df_matched <- brodeur_articles %>%
  # Create temporary clean columns for a fair comparison
  mutate(
    clean_dv = clean_text(dvName, my_custom_words),
    clean_zen = clean_text(zenName, my_custom_words),
    clean_icpsr = clean_text(icpsrName, my_custom_words),
    clean_title = clean_text(title, my_custom_words)
  ) %>%
  # Calculate the match score
  mutate(
    # Jaro-Winkler (jw) outputs a distance between 0 and 1. 
    # 0 = perfect match, 1 = completely different.
    # We subtract from 1 to turn it into a "similarity" percentage (e.g., 1 = 100% match).
    dvMatch = 1 - stringdist(clean_dv, clean_title, method = "jw"),
    zenMatch = 1 - stringdist(clean_zen, clean_title, method = "jw"),
    icpsrMatch = 1 - stringdist(clean_icpsr, clean_title, method = "jw")
  ) %>%
  # Drop the temporary clean columns so your final dataset stays neat
  select(-clean_dv, -clean_title, -clean_zen, clean_icpsr)


#write.csv(df_matched, "articlesWithMatches.csv")


hist(df_matched$dvMatch)
hist(df_matched$icpsrMatch)
hist(df_matched$zenMatch)

p1 <- df_matched %>%

#ggsave("harvardfuzzymatch.png", width = 7, height = 4)

p2 <- df_matched %>%

  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 1), ylim = c(0, 200)) +

p3 <- df_matched %>%
```

## t test

```{r}
df_matched <- df_matched %>%
  mutate(rep_files_exist = case_when(
    dvMatch >= 0.795 ~ 1,
    dvMatch >= 0 ~ 0,
    .default = NA
  ))

df_joined <- brodeur %>%
  left_join(df_matched, by = "title")
df_joined$rep_files_exist[is.na(df_joined$rep_files_exist)] <- 0

summary(df_joined$rep_files_exist)

summary(df_joined$t_orig)
```
